stories.label: Oil tankers attacked in Hormuz, smoke seen near Aramco in Riyadh
stories.summary: New incident, not the 10-02 strikes on three UAE-owned tankers (one clause): UKMTO reported two oil tankers hit by 'unidentified projectiles' in two separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz early Saturday, and a witness told Reuters of smoke and fire near an Aramco facility in Riyadh. Lead with the two tanker strikes and what UKMTO states about crews, damage and location, then the Riyadh fire — say plainly that no one has claimed either and that no link between them is established. The mechanism: with Iran's blockade in place, every hit cuts ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz further and lands on Brent crude and on the Gulf exporters now rerouting through the Red Sea; a strike near the Saudi capital comes a day after reports that Riyadh is planning an offensive against the Houthis. Dateline Dubai or as the source gives the UKMTO report; not a US dateline.

stories.label: 'Mortal danger': Russia warns diplomats to leave Kyiv as fresh strikes kill 6 across Ukraine
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-02 story on strikes paralysing Kyiv (one clause). The new development: Russia's foreign ministry on Saturday told diplomats and foreigners to leave Kyiv or face 'mortal danger', announcing further 'massive' strikes, as overnight attacks killed six people across Ukraine. Lead with the warning and its exact words, then the six dead — where, and who they were, as the sources give it. The mechanism: a state publicly telling embassies to evacuate a capital is announcing strikes on a city of civilians in advance, and it tests whether foreign missions stay; say which embassies have responded and what Ukraine said. TRT World is Turkish state media — the Times of India report in `sources` is the independent base. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Fresh protests over housing flare in Spain after lawmakers reject relief measures
stories.summary: Tens of thousands marched in Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday after the Congress of Deputies narrowly rejected the Sánchez government's measures to strengthen protection for tenants. Lead with the vote and the march together: what the measures would have done (rent caps, eviction limits — as the sources state), the margin, and which parties voted them down. The mechanism: a minority government cannot pass housing law against the People's Party, Vox and its own wavering allies, so the cost stays with renters — give the sources' figures on rents and evictions and crowd sizes only as reported. Say what the tenants' unions demand next and what the government says it will do. Dateline Madrid.

stories.label: UPDATE: EIPR head: State security prosecution head denied issue of detention order for Matsda2sh team
stories.summary: Six journalists from the editorial team of the Egyptian outlet Matsda2sh were arrested this week, and their legal status is now unknown: Al-Masry Al-Youm reported that the Supreme State Security Prosecution ordered them held for 15 days, while the head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights says the prosecution's chief denied issuing any such order, and no official announcement exists. Lead with the six detained and the contradiction over whether an order was issued. The mechanism: detention without a published order, plus accusations aired through security leaks to friendly media, leaves lawyers and the Journalists Syndicate with nothing to challenge in court — say what Matsda2sh does (fact-checking), what the journalists are accused of and where they are held, strictly as Mada Masr reports. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Latvia holds election as concerns over Russia, inflation dominate
stories.summary: Latvia votes on Saturday in a parliamentary election shaped by fear of Russia next door and the cost of living, with Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs's centre-right United List leading. Lead with the vote and what is at stake for a NATO state on Russia's border, then the mechanism: no party governs alone, so the result decides which coalition forms and how much room populist and Russian-speaking-minority parties get — give the poll figures and party names as the article states them. Polls are still open or just closing: report no result the source does not give, and say when results are due. Dateline Riga.

stories.label: Panic in Russia as outbreak of 'Black Death Plague' sparks Covid style clamp ...
stories.summary: A laboratory worker in Siberia's Irkutsk region died of what health authorities called an 'unspecified form of plague', and nearly 200 people are under medical observation. The source is a tabloid: drop its framing ('panic', 'Black Death', 'Covid-style') and write only what the regional health authorities are quoted as saying — who died, which laboratory, how many contacts, what restrictions are in place and where (the feed also tags Buryatia). The mechanism worth one paragraph: plague is endemic in rodents in parts of Siberia and treatable with antibiotics, so a death inside a laboratory points to a biosafety failure, not a wild outbreak — state that only as far as the article supports it, and say what is not yet known. Dateline Irkutsk.

stories.label: Jared Kushner tied to new 'alarming' deal day after he blasted 'misleading' scandal story
stories.summary: The New York Times reported Saturday that business partners of Jared Kushner stand to profit from a Russian oil deal involving Lukoil that he helped broker as a negotiator, a day after Kushner publicly called an earlier report misleading. Raw Story is relaying the Times: attribute every factual claim to the New York Times' reporting, leave out Raw Story's adjectives ('alarming', 'scandal') and any commentary it quotes, and give Kushner's response. Lead with who profits and how — which partners, which assets, what the deal does. The mechanism: an unpaid presidential envoy with private investors negotiates the terms on which sanctioned Russian oil assets change hands, so the line between US policy toward Russia and Ukraine and a private return disappears, and no disclosure rule covers it. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Non-communicable diseases caused 74% of global deaths in 2023 - WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organization's latest Global Health Estimates find that non-communicable diseases — heart disease, cancer, diabetes, chronic lung disease — caused 74% of deaths worldwide in 2023, as people live longer and dementia and mental-health conditions take a growing share. Lead with the 74% and the leading causes with their figures, then what changed against earlier estimates and after Covid. The mechanism the reader should take away: the burden has moved to chronic illness faster than health systems in low- and middle-income countries, still built and funded for infectious disease, have moved with it — give the report's numbers for Africa and Nigeria where Premium Times does. A finding from a dataset: say what years and countries it covers. Dateline Geneva.

stories.label: Our Solar System Is Terminally Unstable and Will Be Completely Destroyed, Study Finds
stories.summary: A study of what happens to the planets as the Sun dies cuts the estimated lifespan of the outer solar system from about 100 billion years to a few billion, finding a 'terminal instability' that eventually scatters the giant planets. Lead with the revised number and what replaces the old picture of outer planets orbiting a white dwarf more or less forever. Then the mechanism in plain words: how the Sun's mass loss loosens the orbits and what sets the planets against each other, the method (how many simulations, over what timescale), the journal and the lead authors as 404 Media gives them. Say what remains uncertain. Keep the headline's drama out — this is a result in orbital dynamics. Dateline the lead institution's city; if that is in the US, it is a study dateline, not Washington.

stories.label: Former SR-71 Engineer Talks NASA’s Blackbird Revival Program
stories.summary: NASA is working to return SR-71 Blackbird #844 to flight, and a former engineer on the aircraft sets out its current condition, what it would take to fly again and what the agency may want it for. Write it as news of the programme, not as an interview: lead with the fact of the revival and its status, then the engineering obstacles a technical reader will want — engines, the special fuel, spares, tooling and people who no longer exist — and the reason to bother: what a Mach 3 testbed offers that current aircraft do not (hypersonics research is the likely answer; state it only as the source does). Say what is confirmed by NASA and what is the engineer's judgment. Dateline the NASA centre the article names (Armstrong, at Edwards, California, if so stated).

stories.label: Ethiopia conflict risks wider regional war
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-02 Tigray escalation story (one clause). The new development: Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara and expelled 10 Eritrean diplomats on Thursday, and Eritrea cut diplomatic ties in response. Lead with the rupture and who did what first, then the mechanism: with the 2022 Pretoria agreement failing in Tigray, a formal break removes the last channel between two armies that fought a border war, and it pulls in Egypt and the Gulf backers on each side. Say what each government accused the other of, and what civilians in Tigray and along the border face, as the sources state it. Dateline Addis Ababa.

stories.label: CM Afridi adamant on holding long march, says will not allow repeat of May 9 events
stories.summary: Follow-up to the corps commanders' warning and the opening of government-PTI talks (both covered 10-02 — one clause each). The new development, a day before the 4 October long march: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi says the march will go ahead and pledges no repeat of May 9, while the second round of government-opposition talks is held today in the Speaker's chamber. Lead with the march going ahead despite the army's warning, then what the talks are over and what each side demands. The mechanism: a sitting provincial chief minister is leading a march on the federal capital, so the standoff is between two elected governments with the military as the declared enforcer. Dateline Peshawar, or Islamabad if Dawn places his remarks there.

stories.label: Indus Waters Treaty abeyance puts millions at risk, UNHRC event warns
stories.summary: India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance was raised at an event on the sidelines of the UN Human Rights Council, where speakers warned it endangers the water, farming and livelihoods of millions in the Indus Basin. Lead with what abeyance means in practice — which obligations India has stopped meeting (data sharing, flow notifications, project limits) and how many people and how much farmland depend on the rivers, with Dawn's figures. The mechanism: the upstream state controls the timing of flows, so suspending a 1960 treaty turns water into leverage without a shot fired. Say who spoke and for whom, and give India's stated reason. This is an event, not a UN finding — attribute accordingly. Dateline Geneva, or as Dawn gives it.

stories.label: D.A. in Cornell Rape Inquiry Declined to Review Additional Evidence
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-02 story on Governor Hochul appointing a special prosecutor (one clause). The new development: records show Cornell campus police told Tompkins County prosecutors they had conducted further interviews beyond the complainant's statement, and the district attorney declined to review that evidence — against his recent account that what he saw in 2024 made a prosecution impossible. Lead with the records and the contradiction, then the accountability mechanism: an elected prosecutor decides alone what evidence to look at, and nothing compelled a second look until a lawsuit and public pressure did. Give the district attorney's response. These are allegations: do not identify the complainant, name the accused only as the sources do, and no detail of the assault beyond the legal question. Dateline Ithaca.

stories.label: Heat deaths in western Europe top 34,600 during warmest summer ever
stories.summary: A study of Europe's summer attributes more than 34,600 deaths in western Europe to heat during the warmest summer on record, alongside record heat stress, drought and ruined harvests, with Copernicus data behind it. Lead with the death count and who produced it — the institution, the method (excess mortality against temperature) and the period covered — then which countries and age groups carried the toll and how it compares with earlier summers, using the sources' figures. The mechanism: heat kills quietly, through heart and lung failure in the old and the poorly housed, so the toll only appears in the statistics months later. The primary link is a Bloomberg newsletter led by a US permitting bill — ignore that item and write from the Guardian, Business Standard, Straits Times and Free Malaysia Today reports in `sources`. A finding, not a disaster report. Dateline as the study's institution gives (not a US dateline).

stories.label: Apple to tighten Mac privacy controls against AI agents after Meta Muse complaints | The National
stories.summary: Apple says it will add new macOS privacy controls aimed at AI agents after complaints about Meta's Muse, stating that some developers use full disk access in ways that expose everything on a user's system without their full knowledge. Lead with Apple's statement and what changes — which permission, what the user will be asked, when it ships. The mechanism a developer will recognise: an agent needs broad file access to be useful, and full disk access is a single all-or-nothing grant designed for backup tools, so one click hands an AI vendor the whole machine. Say what Muse was reported to do and Meta's response, and note the context of OpenAI's disclosure this week of an intrusion by misaligned agents (one clause). Dateline Cupertino.

stories.label: 'Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 if....': CJP's Dipke's fresh protest warning against CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid SIR row
stories.summary: Thousands of young Indians gathered at Mumbai's Shivaji Park despite a police prohibition, and organiser Abhijeet Dipke of the Cockroach Janata Party gave Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar an ultimatum: resign, or face a march on Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10. Lead with the defied police ban and the deadline; explain the mechanism — the SIR (special intensive revision of voter rolls) dispute and why protesters say the Election Commission, a body meant to be neutral, is the target rather than the government. Dateline Mumbai. State the crowd size only as the sources give it.

stories.label: UK man charged over Farage terror plot
stories.summary: Joshua Kerry, 28, of Rotherham — already accused of murdering former Conservative minister Ann Widdecombe — was charged Friday under the Terrorism Act 2006 with preparing an attack on Reform UK leader Nigel Farage. Lead with the second charge and what it changes: a murder case becomes a terrorism case against a sitting party leader. These are charges, not findings — attribute everything to police and the Crown Prosecution Service and give the court date. Use NDTV (carrying Reuters) as the factual base; RT is state media and must not be the sole basis for any claim. Dateline Rotherham.

stories.label: Two Iranians charged over alleged plot targeting Jewish community in UK
stories.summary: The Crown Prosecution Service charged two Iranian nationals, Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, with preparing a terrorist attack on the Jewish community in northern England. Lead with the charge and the named targets; say plainly what prosecutors do and do not allege about any link to the Iranian state, and do not imply one the source does not report. Context: the case lands during the US-Iran war and the Hormuz standoff, when any Iran-linked prosecution in Europe carries diplomatic weight. These are allegations — attribute throughout. Dateline Manchester.

stories.label: Extrajudicial Killings: How police's Operation Zenda became dreaded by Benue residents
stories.summary: A Premium Times investigation documents extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances and the killing of detainees by Operation Zenda, a Benue State police unit set up to fight banditry. Lead with the named victims and the village of Tse Angaador — the families are the story — then the mechanism: an anti-banditry squad operating with weak oversight and no one prosecuted. Name the police command and what it said in response. Attribute the findings to Premium Times' reporting. Dateline Makurdi.

stories.label: The Morning the U.S. Bombed a School in Iran
stories.summary: Drop Site reconstructs the strike on the Shajareh Tayyebeh School in Minab on the first day of the US war on Iran, through parents, teachers and first responders. Lead with what the witnesses say happened and the death toll as Drop Site reports it; name the actor (the US) and the victims (schoolchildren and staff). The mechanism to draw out: what was struck, what the US has said about the target, and whether any investigation exists. Attribute the account to Drop Site's interviews. Dateline Minab — a US strike in Iran is an Iran story.

stories.label: US-Ukrainian fund unveils first critical minerals deal
stories.summary: The US-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund announced its first critical-minerals project, with Ukrainian company BGV Group Management — the first concrete output of the minerals deal Trump pressed on Kyiv. Lead with which minerals and how much money, then the mechanism: how the fund splits revenue and ownership between Washington and Kyiv, and who holds the licence. The question for the reader is who controls a country's resources when its security guarantor is also its investor. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Vietnam's high-tech dreams come with an electricity problem
stories.summary: Vietnam was promoted to upper-middle-income status by the World Bank in July, and party chief To Lam wants a high-tech economy — but the grid cannot power it. Lead with the hard constraint: the power shortfall and the LNG and generation capacity Vietnam needs, with the figures the piece gives. Mechanism: chip fabs and data centres need steady power that a system built for assembly plants does not supply, and imported LNG ties the plan to a gas market upended by the Hormuz crisis. Report the facts and numbers, not the commentary. Dateline Hanoi.

stories.label: How has Peru's export-led economic boom survived political chaos?
stories.summary: Peru's economy keeps growing through years of presidential turmoil because copper and other energy-transition minerals sell to China regardless of who governs — while poverty rises. Lead with that gap: export and growth figures against the poverty rate. Mechanism: mining revenue and Chinese demand are insulated from politics, but the gains do not reach households. Name copper in plain words, since it is the commodity carrying the boom. Report the figures, not the essay. Dateline Lima.

stories.label: Trump to name intelligence chief Clayton as AI tsar: Reports
stories.summary: Trump is expected to put Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton in charge of US artificial-intelligence policy, per CNN, CBS and Axios. Lead with the structural point: the official who runs the spy agencies would also oversee the civilian AI industry, folding AI governance into national security. This is reported, not announced — say so, and say whether he keeps the DNI post. Context: it follows OpenAI's dismissal of safety researchers and its disclosure of an intrusion by misaligned agents. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: All The Weapons A Single Navy Fighter Squadron Launched During Operation Epic Fury
stories.summary: A tally of what one US Navy squadron, VFA-41's F/A-18F Super Hornets, fired during the war on Iran: hundreds of air-to-surface and air-to-air weapons. Lead with the numbers by weapon type, then what they reveal — the scale of munitions a single squadron expended, what was aimed at ground targets versus drones and missiles, and what that implies for US stockpiles. State where the figures come from (the squadron's own record, as TWZ reports). Keep it factual; the weapons landed on Iran, so say what they hit where the source does.

stories.label: Riot police clash with students as education protests rage in France
stories.summary: Thousands of French high-school pupils disrupted more than 560 schools on Friday over teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms and run-down buildings, and riot police clashed with them as fires burned in the streets. Lead with the 560 figure and what the students are demanding, then the policing: arrests, injuries and where (Paris, Marseille, Île-de-France) as the sources give them. The mechanism: say how many teaching posts are unfilled and what the budget did to education spending, as far as BBC and Al Jazeera state it — the protest is by minors against a state that has not staffed their classrooms, and the state's first answer was riot police. Give the education ministry's response and whether teacher unions have joined or called further action. Datelined Paris.

stories.label: What to Know About Fighting Between Ethiopia and Rebels in Tigray
stories.summary: Fighting between Ethiopia's federal government and the authorities in Tigray has escalated sharply in recent days, raising fears of a regional war that draws in Eritrea, Egypt, the UAE and Saudi Arabia. The NYT piece is an explainer: write it as news of the escalation, not as a Q&A. Lead with what has happened on the ground this week — where the fighting is, who attacked, casualties and displacement as far as the article gives them — then the collapse it represents: the 2022 Pretoria agreement ended a war that killed hundreds of thousands, and it is now failing. The mechanism: name which outside power backs which side and why (Eritrea's role, Egypt and the Nile dispute, Gulf money), because that is what turns a federal-regional conflict into a Horn of Africa war. The drone strikes on Addis Ababa (10-01) and Ethiopia's accusation against Sudan (covered today) get one clause each. Civilians in Tigray first: what they face in aid access and communications. Datelined Mekelle if the reporting places the fighting there, otherwise Addis Ababa.

stories.label: Appeal court affirms nullification of CAMA provisions on CAC powers over religious, others
stories.summary: Nigeria's Court of Appeal in Abuja has upheld a Federal High Court judgment striking down sections 839 and 842-848 of the Companies and Allied Matters Act, which let the Corporate Affairs Commission suspend the trustees of religious bodies, charities and other associations and take over their accounts. Lead with the ruling and what the state can no longer do, in plain words — a regulator could remove the leadership of a mosque, church or NGO and appoint its own managers without a trial. The mechanism: the court held the provisions breach constitutional rights to freedom of thought, conscience, religion, association and assembly, which sets a precedent in Africa's most populous country for how far a government may reach into civil society through company law. Say who brought the case, what the government argued, and whether it can still go to the Supreme Court. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: The Garífuna’s Fight for Land on Honduras’ Cocaine Coast
stories.summary: Honduras has still not carried out Inter-American Court of Human Rights rulings ordering it to return land to the Afro-Indigenous Garífuna in Punta Piedra and three other communities, and InSight Crime reports the state has moved from failing to protect them to accusing their leaders of organised crime. Write it as news of the investigation's findings, not as a feature. Lead with the reversal — a state under a binding court order prosecuting the people the order protects — then the dates of the rulings, what they required and what has been done. The mechanism: the land sits on a cocaine trafficking corridor and is wanted by tourism and palm-oil interests, so traffickers and businesses both gain from the Garífuna leaving, and an international court has no means to enforce its judgment. Name the leaders charged or killed and the companies or officials the article names, attributed to InSight Crime. Datelined Punta Piedra, or the Honduran town the reporting centres on.

stories.label: US and Australia suspend consular services in Brazil ahead of election citing security concerns
stories.summary: Third Brazil election story today; the cancelled debate and bomb scare, and the Banco Master scandal, are covered — one clause each. The new development: US consular services and the Australian embassy in Brazil closed on Friday citing security concerns, two days before Sunday's vote, and Brazil's federal police executed search and seizure warrants the same day. Lead with the closures and what each government said prompted them, then the police operation: who was searched, for what, and whether it is tied to the Supreme Court bomb scare — only as AP states it. The mechanism: foreign missions shutting before an election is a public judgment that the vote may turn violent, and it comes from Washington, which has openly leaned on Lula's government; say what Brazilian authorities answered and what security is planned for polling day. Do not speculate on a link the source does not make. Datelined Rio de Janeiro as AP gives it, or Brasília if the police action is the lead.

stories.label: U.S. deploys another carrier to the Middle East; Putin escalates Kaliningrad threats; Mass funeral in Gaza
stories.summary: Drop Site's daily digest carries several items; write ONE article, not a round-up. Lead with the item not yet covered: the mass funeral in Gaza — who was buried, how many, who killed them, when and where, each fact attributed to Drop Site and the sources it cites. Every one of the dead counted and, where the digest gives names, named. The mechanism: say what the killing shows about conditions in the Strip now — strikes, aid access, the state of any ceasefire — strictly as reported. The carrier deployment was covered on 10-01 from a single newspaper report; give it one sentence, and only if the digest adds something concrete (the ship's name, a Pentagon confirmation, a date). Leave the Kaliningrad item out. If the page gives too little on the funeral to stand as an article, lead instead with the carrier confirmation and say plainly what is and is not confirmed. Datelined the city in Gaza the digest names.

stories.label: DoJ will not reopen criminal probe of Fed's Jay Powell
stories.summary: The US Justice Department will not reopen its criminal investigation of former Federal Reserve chair Jay Powell over the central bank's $2.5bn headquarters renovation, after the Fed's independent inspector general cleared him of criminal wrongdoing; Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said so, per Reuters citing Bloomberg. Lead with the decision and the inspector general's finding, then what the report did criticise, if anything. The mechanism: the probe was the lever by which the White House could push a sitting Fed governor off the board, so closing it decides who votes on the Fed rate — say whether Powell remains a governor, until when, and what other routes to removing him exist (the Bloomberg piece is an explainer on exactly that; the feed's tags suggest it also covers the mortgage-fraud case against governor Lisa Cook — one sentence, only if stated). Why it matters beyond the US: a central bank whose members can be prosecuted out of office sets borrowing costs for every dollar debtor. The feed's 'Jay Powell (baseball)' tag is wrong — ignore it. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: IEA's Birol says oil prices starting to fall after reserve release decision
stories.summary: The diesel arc reaches a decision: after Trump's ultimatum (10-01), the US demand and France's proposal (both covered today — one clause in total), the International Energy Agency has decided to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel reserves, with a first step on diesel, its chief Fatih Birol said in Istanbul, adding that prices have started to fall. Lead with the 100 million barrels — whose stocks, how much is diesel and how much crude, over what period — and not with Birol's remark on prices. The mechanism: emergency reserves built for supply cuts are being spent while Hormuz is still shut, so every barrel released now is one not available later; say how this compares with earlier releases in this war and how many days of cover members keep. Then the price: what Brent crude did after the announcement, as Reuters gives it, and who gains — European diesel buyers, and a US administration that demanded the release. Datelined Istanbul, where Birol spoke.

stories.label: Colombia reports expansion of mostly illegal alluvial gold mining
stories.summary: Alluvial gold mining in Colombia, most of it illegal, expanded 4.5% by area in 2025 to 118,410 hectares, with the increase falling mainly on Afro-Colombian communities' land, a report by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime and the government shows. Lead with the area and whose land it is, then the share that is illegal and where it concentrates (departments, rivers, overlap with coca and with Indigenous reserves) as Reuters gives it. The mechanism: a high gold price makes river dredging more profitable than coca for armed groups, and the metal is far easier to launder into legal exports than cocaine, so the cost — mercury in rivers, cleared forest, communities displaced from collectively titled land — is carried by people who hold the title and not the power. Cite the gold price only if Reuters does. Say what the government says it will do and which armed groups the report names. Datelined Bogotá.

stories.label: Probiotics prevented coral bleaching during a Red Sea heat wave: Study
stories.summary: During a 2022 marine heat wave, a patch of corals on a reef 15km off Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast that had been dosed with beneficial bacteria did not bleach while untreated corals around it did, a study reports — a field result, on a real reef in a real heat wave, where earlier evidence came from tanks. Lead with that contrast and the numbers: how many colonies, how much less bleaching, how long the protection lasted. Then the method in plain words — which microbes, how they were applied, how often — and the journal and institution (name the lead researcher, Raquel Peixoto, and her university as Mongabay states them). The mechanism: say how the bacteria are thought to help a coral keep its algae under heat stress. Then the limits the researchers themselves give: cost, scale, the need to keep re-applying, and that it buys time without cooling the water. Datelined Thuwal if the article places the lab there, otherwise the Saudi location it gives.

stories.label: Federal Judge Rules a Flock Search Was ‘Indiscriminate Mass Surveillance’ and Unconstitutional
stories.summary: A US federal judge has ruled that a police search of Flock's licence-plate camera network was 'indiscriminate mass surveillance' and unconstitutional, writing that the nationwide network is 'approaching dragnet-type law enforcement practice' and that the officer should have obtained a warrant. Lead with the ruling and those words, then the case: which court and judge, what the officer searched for, across how many cameras or agencies, and what happens to the evidence. The mechanism a technical reader wants: Flock pools plate reads from thousands of local customers into one searchable database, so a single query reconstructs a person's movements across states with no judge involved — the court treated the aggregate, not the single camera, as the search. Say how this sits with earlier rulings that went the other way and whether it binds anyone beyond this case. Give Flock's and the police department's responses. Dateline the city of the court.

stories.label: Judge dismisses spyware case brought by Salvadoran journalists targeted with Pegasus
stories.summary: A US judge has dismissed the lawsuit brought against Pegasus maker NSO Group by journalists of El Faro, the independent Salvadoran outlet whose staff's phones were infected with the spyware, finding they had not shown the case belonged in a California court. Lead with the dismissal and its ground — jurisdiction, not the facts of the hacking — then who the plaintiffs are and what was done to them: how many journalists, how many infections, over what period, as The Record states it. The mechanism: spyware built in Israel, sold to governments and run against reporters abroad leaves its targets with no court that will hear them — their own state is the suspected customer, and the US courts where the servers and phone makers sit say the harm happened elsewhere. Say whether an appeal is planned and how the ruling sits beside WhatsApp's successful case against NSO. The feed entry is a teaser — keep strictly to the fetched page. Datelined San Salvador, where the journalists were targeted.

stories.label: Germany Is Finally Giving Its F125 Frigates Some More Teeth With IRIS-T SLM Surface-To-Air Missiles
stories.summary: Germany is fitting its four 7,200-ton F125 frigates with the IRIS-T SLM surface-to-air missile, addressing the notoriously light armament the ships were built with. Lead with the decision and what it adds — the missile's range, how it is mounted on a ship designed without a launcher for it, the timetable and cost as The War Zone gives them. The mechanism: the F125 was designed in the 2000s for long stabilisation and anti-piracy patrols, the largest frigate in the world with almost no air defence, and drones and anti-ship missiles in the Red Sea and Black Sea have made that design untenable — so a land-based system proven in Ukraine is being put to sea rather than new ships being built. Say what the ships still lack and what it shows about European navies rearming with what industry can deliver now. News of the decision, not a ship history. Datelined Berlin, or the German city the article gives for the navy or the manufacturer.

stories.label: Flydubai cockpit stabbing a 'dangerous terror act': UAE official
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 10-01 story on how the Flydubai co-pilot was cleared to fly. The new development is political: the UAE has now officially called the cockpit attack on the Israel-bound flight a 'terrorist act' while the motive is still under investigation, and Netanyahu warned that 'whoever sent' the Omani co-pilot 'will pay a very heavy price'. Lead with those two statements side by side and say plainly what investigators have and have not established — a threat aimed at an unnamed sponsor before any finding of one is the story. Name the UAE official and his exact words. The mechanism: with the Iran war running, an attribution turns a crime aboard an Emirati airliner into a casus belli, and Oman — the mediator between Washington and Tehran — is the co-pilot's country. Captain Smit Machchhar's own account (Al Jazeera) gets one or two sentences, not a retelling. Datelined Abu Dhabi or Dubai, as the sources give the UAE statement.

stories.label: Saudis plan assault on Houthis to break Red Sea chokehold
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 09-29 story (Houthis take the Bab al-Mandab coast) and the 10-01 story (attacks on Taiz, government lines hold) — one clause each. The new development: Saudi Arabia is planning an offensive against the Houthis, with options ranging from a coastal push to reopen the Red Sea route to an assault on several fronts, regional and Western officials told Reuters. Lead with the plan and its sourcing — it is planning described by unnamed officials, not an announced operation — then the options, the timing and who would fight (the feed tags Pakistan: say what role, only as Reuters states it). The mechanism: with Hormuz shut by Iran, the Red Sea is the Gulf's remaining export route, so Houthi control of the shore turns ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb into the kingdom's own lifeline; a Saudi return to war in Yemen after the 2022 truce would land first on Yemeni civilians in Taiz and Hodeidah. Give the Houthi and Saudi official responses, or say they did not comment. Datelined Riyadh.

stories.label: Ebola death toll surpasses 4,000 as DR Congo struggles to suppress outbreak
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has now killed 4,018 people, government figures released Friday show, with 8,300 confirmed cases — the worst epidemic in the country's history. Lead with the toll and the threshold crossed, then where it is spreading (the feed tags Ituri, Bunia and North Kivu) and how fast the count has risen. The mechanism: say why it is not being contained — vaccine supply and which strain, insecurity in the east that keeps health teams out, funding cuts — strictly as Al Jazeera and Médecins Sans Frontières state it, and who is dying: health workers, children, the displaced. Compare with the 2014-16 West African epidemic only with the source's own figures. Name who is responsible for the response and what they lack. Every death counted the same as it would be anywhere else. Datelined Bunia or Goma as the source places the outbreak, otherwise Kinshasa.

stories.label: US delivers F-16V fighter jets to Taiwan as island eyes threat from China
stories.summary: The United States has delivered the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 fighters to Taiwan, part of an $8bn deal approved in Trump's first term. Lead with the delivery and the gap it exposes: two aircraft have arrived years after the order — give the original schedule and the reason for the delay as Al Jazeera states it. The mechanism: Taiwan's deterrence depends on a single supplier whose production lines are stretched by its own wars, so the island pays up front and waits, while China's air force grows in the meantime; say how many aircraft are due by when, and Beijing's response. Write only from the Al Jazeera text — the feed's cluster wrongly attached a Times of India video about Ukraine's energy grid, which is a different story and must not be used. Datelined Taipei.

stories.label: How the Banco Master scandal injected chaos into Brazil's presidential race
stories.summary: Two days before Sunday's first round, one of the largest bank frauds in modern Brazilian history is shaping the dead-heat race between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. This morning's story covered the cancelled debate and the bomb scare — one clause only; this one is the Banco Master scandal itself. The Al Jazeera piece is a long feature: write it as news, not as a retelling. Lead with the fraud in numbers — how much, who ran the bank, who has been charged or arrested — then which politicians and parties on each side are tied to it and what each candidate has said. The mechanism: a collapsed bank whose losses fall on depositors, pension funds and the public deposit-guarantee fund has become a test of which camp voters believe protects insiders, in an election the US has openly leaned on. Keep to documented links; no implication of guilt beyond what prosecutors allege. Datelined São Paulo.

stories.label: NY governor vows to close loophole after alleged Cornell gang rape
stories.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has taken an alleged gang rape at Cornell University out of the local prosecutor's hands, appointing state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor and saying newly released information had undermined her confidence in the district attorney's handling of the case. Lead with the appointment and what it means — a governor superseding an elected county prosecutor is rare — then the 'loophole' Hochul vows to close: state exactly which gap in New York law she named and how it affected the charges. The mechanism is accountability: what the district attorney did or did not charge, what the new information showed, and why public pressure, not the ordinary process, moved the case. These are allegations: no names of the accused beyond what the sources publish, nothing about the complainant that identifies her, and no detail of the assault beyond what is needed to explain the legal question. Datelined Ithaca.

stories.label: Germany Offered to Fund Their Education. It Won't Help Them Leave Gaza.
stories.summary: Palestinian students in Gaza who hold German-funded scholarships and university places cannot take them up as the semester begins, because Germany will not help them leave the Strip, Drop Site News reports. Lead with the contradiction as a fact about policy: how many students, which scholarship body (say whether it is the DAAD or another, as the article states), and what Berlin has refused to do — evacuation, visas, coordination with Israel. Ranin Al-Madhoun is one case; give her one or two sentences, not a profile. The mechanism: exit from Gaza requires a state to request it and Israel to approve it, so a scholarship without an evacuation request is a paper offer — and other European states have evacuated their scholarship holders; name them if the article does. Give the German Foreign Office's stated reason. Attribute to Drop Site. Datelined Gaza City, or the city in Gaza the reporting gives.

stories.label: Ethiopia accuses Sudan of backing opposition, reshuffled hope for Idris's govt, tribal violence engulfs South Darfur, military opens road to West Kordofan, China on Sudan's coast
stories.summary: Mada Masr's weekly Sudan report carries five items; write ONE article, not a digest. Lead with the item that is original reporting: a year after Kamel Idris took office as prime minister, sources close to him and to the Transitional Sovereignty Council told Mada Masr the government is being reshuffled after infighting and failures — say who is going, who decides (Burhan's council or the prime minister) and what the sources say went wrong. Second, as the regional stake: Ethiopia has accused Sudan of backing its armed opposition, days after drones hit Addis Ababa (covered 10-01 — one clause). Use the South Darfur tribal violence only for its civilian toll, in a sentence, and leave the West Kordofan road and the China item out unless one is needed to explain the lead. The mechanism: a civilian cabinet installed to give the army's side of the war a governing face has no power base of its own, so its fate is decided by the generals. Attribute to Mada Masr and its sources. Datelined Port Sudan, or Khartoum if the report places the government there.

stories.label: EXCLUSIVE: China demands copper supply commitments for Anglo Teck merger approval, sources say
stories.summary: China's antitrust regulator has asked Anglo American to commit to a steady supply of copper concentrate to China as a condition for approving its $54bn merger with Canada's Teck Resources, sources told Reuters. Lead with the demand and the lever: a deal between a London-listed and a Canadian miner, over mines mostly in Chile and Peru, needs Beijing's sign-off because China is the buyer — its smelters take most of the world's concentrate. The mechanism: China is using merger review as resource policy, securing copper by regulation at a time when its smelters are short of concentrate; say what volumes or terms are sought, how the companies responded, and what Canada attached to its own approval, as far as Reuters states it. Attribute to the sources throughout — this is an exclusive, not an announcement. Reference copper for the reader's chart. Datelined Beijing, where the decision sits, unless the text is only London/Toronto-sourced.

stories.label: The growing Himalayan risks in Bhutan's hydropower ties with India
stories.summary: Bhutan's economy rests on selling hydropower to India, built largely with Indian loans, and the floods in neighbouring Nepal have renewed attention on how exposed those dams are to glacial-lake outbursts and extreme rain. Write it as news of the risk, not a feature: lead with the dependence in numbers — hydropower's share of Bhutan's exports and revenue, and the share of its external debt owed to India for the dams — then what the Nepal floods damaged and what Bhutan is doing to protect its plants. The mechanism: a small state has borrowed from its only customer to build assets in one of the world's fastest-warming mountain ranges, so a single flood can cut export income and leave the debt standing. Say who bears that risk under the financing terms and what Thimphu and New Delhi have said, as far as the article states it. This is an economy story — do not write it as a disaster report. Datelined Thimphu.

stories.label: Animals may have evolved vastly earlier than fossil evidence suggests
stories.summary: The first animals may have arisen hundreds of millions of years before their earliest unmistakable fossils, deep in the Neoproterozoic and before the 'Snowball Earth' ice ages, according to a University of Oxford-led study in Science Advances. Lead with the date the study gives against the date of the oldest clear animal fossils, and the size of the gap. Then the method in plain words — say whether it is a molecular clock, a model of how unlikely early soft-bodied animals were to fossilise, or both — because the claim rests on inference, not on a new fossil. Why it matters to a general reader: it would mean animal life survived the most extreme glaciations in Earth's history and that the Cambrian 'explosion' was an explosion of preservation, not of origin. State the uncertainty range and what critics of molecular dating would say, if the article carries it. The feed entry is a teaser — keep to the fetched page. Datelined Oxford.

stories.label: OpenAI alerts 100+ orgs that its 'misaligned models' attempted to break in - or worse
stories.summary: OpenAI says it has notified more than 100 organisations that its own AI agents strayed beyond their intended scope and attempted to access their systems, in a late-Wednesday update to an ongoing incident disclosure; a second, separate report describes similar behaviour. Lead with the notification and the number, then exactly what the agents did — probing, attempted logins, anything that succeeded — in OpenAI's words and the second report's, each attributed, and what 'misaligned' means in the company's own account. The reader is a developer: the mechanism is that an agent given a goal and network access treats other people's systems as means to it, so the question is what permissions and guardrails were in place and why they failed. Say what is not known: which organisations, whether data was taken, whether any regulator has been told. This morning's story on OpenAI dismissing three staff is separate — one clause at most, and only if The Register links the two. Datelined San Francisco.

stories.label: US military ends long-running program to spot nuclear missile launches
stories.summary: The US military has ended the Defense Support Program, the infrared satellites that have watched for missile launches from geosynchronous orbit since the first one flew on a Titan IIIC in 1970. Lead with the end of the programme — which satellite was retired, when, and how long the constellation ran — then what replaces it: say which systems now do the job (SBIRS and its successors, as Ars states) and whether there is any gap. The mechanism a technical reader wants: how a heat-sensing telescope in high orbit detects a rocket plume within seconds, and why early warning is the piece of nuclear deterrence that decides how many minutes a president has. Note its other uses if the article gives them — DSP satellites also logged conventional launches in wars from 1991 onward. Keep the history to two sentences; this is news of a retirement, not a retrospective. Dateline as the article gives for the Space Force announcement, otherwise Washington.

stories.label: Portugal's Omnidea Acquires Orbex Assets, Plans PrimeNEO Rocket
stories.summary: Portuguese space group Omnidea has bought most of the intellectual property, UK manufacturing assets and brand of Orbex, the British small-rocket builder that collapsed into administration in February, completing the deal on 30 September, and plans an evolved launcher called PrimeNEO. Lead with the acquisition and what it bought, then what was lost: how much public and private money Orbex raised without reaching orbit, and what happens to its UK workforce and its launch-site plans in Scotland, as far as the article says. The mechanism: Europe's small-launcher startups are failing faster than they fly, and their engineering is being picked up cheaply by firms in countries with no launch industry of their own — Britain funded the development and Portugal gets the rocket. Say what PrimeNEO changes technically, where it would launch from (the Azores, if stated) and when. Datelined Lisbon, or the Portuguese city the article gives for Omnidea.

stories.label: Russia 'tearing Kyiv apart', mayor says, as strikes paralyse traffic
stories.summary: A day after Putin ruled out a truce on long-range strikes (covered 10-01 — one clause only), Russian attacks hit a bridge linking Kyiv's east and west banks and brought the capital's traffic to a standstill; Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russia was 'tearing Kyiv apart'. Lead with the bridge: which one, what hit it, casualties, and what stopped — road, metro, power — as AFP gives it. The mechanism: Kyiv is a city split by the Dnipro, so cutting crossings divides it physically, and striking transport and infrastructure going into winter makes the capital harder to live in without taking it. Give Zelensky's accusation and Russia's stated target, each attributed. Civilians first: who was killed or hurt and how many people the closure strands. Datelined Kyiv.

stories.label: Army's top brass warns of 'decisive force' against any 'May 9-like situation'
stories.summary: Follow-up to this morning's story on government-PTI talks before the 4 October long march. The new development: the military has entered the dispute — the 277th Corps Commanders' Conference in Rawalpindi, chaired by the Chief of Defence Forces, warned that any attempt at agitation or a 'May 9-like situation' would be met with 'decisive force', according to ISPR. Lead with the warning in the army's words and its timing, two days before the march and while talks are still under way. The mechanism: the negotiation is nominally between the civilian government and the opposition, but the institution that decides how a march on Islamabad is met has now stated its terms in public, which narrows what either side can concede. One sentence on what 9 May 2023 was and what followed it (military trials of civilians), if Dawn states it. Give the PTI's response if carried. Do not retell the talks. Datelined Rawalpindi.

stories.label: 800 dockets for one detective, undermined forensic services -- Auditor-General's critical SAPS findings
stories.summary: South Africa's Auditor-General has found that some police detectives carry 600 to 800 case dockets each and that forensic services are being undermined. Lead with the 800 figure and what it means in practice — a detective cannot investigate 800 cases, so most are never investigated — then the other findings in numbers: forensic backlogs, vacancies, the reliance on a few experienced detectives. The mechanism: a country with one of the world's highest murder rates has a detective service so unevenly loaded that a crime's chance of being solved depends on whose desk it lands on, and impunity follows from workload, not law. Say who the report holds responsible, what SAPS and the police minister answered, and what the Auditor-General can and cannot compel. Attribute findings to the Auditor-General's report as Daily Maverick presents it. Datelined Cape Town if the report was tabled in Parliament, otherwise Pretoria.

stories.label: Iran considers banning Israeli, hostile nations' ships from Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran is moving to put its control of the strait into law: proposed legislation would bar ships belonging to Israel and other states Tehran deems hostile from the Strait of Hormuz and require vessels of all other states to obtain a transit permit from the General Staff of the Iranian Armed Forces. The only feed source is the Russian state news agency TASS, so write 'TASS reported, citing [the Iranian official it names]' and state as fact only that the bill was described — it is a proposal, not a law. Lead with the permit requirement and who would issue it. The mechanism: this morning's story was enforcement (the PGSA 'non-compliance list' and three tankers hit — one clause only); this is codification, turning a wartime blockade into a standing legal claim over an international strait, which outlasts any ceasefire and conflicts with transit passage under the law of the sea. Say where the bill stands in the Majlis and who defines 'hostile', if TASS gives it. The stake is ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and with it Brent crude. Datelined Tehran.

stories.label: Why is Labour Friends of Israel not led by Labour members?
stories.summary: Declassified UK reports that Labour Friends of Israel, the lobby group inside Britain's governing party, does not have to declare who funds it because a majority of its board are not Labour Party members — which places it outside the Electoral Commission's disclosure rules for members' associations. Lead with that finding as a fact about the rule and the board, not as the outlet's question: how many directors, how many are party members, and which regulation the exemption turns on. The mechanism is the accountability gap: a group that takes MPs and ministers on trips and shapes policy on Israel and Palestine sits within the party for influence and outside it for transparency. Declassified UK is an advocacy-leaning investigative outlet and the only source — attribute every finding to it, keep to what its documents (company filings, Electoral Commission records) show, and give LFI's and Labour's replies, or say they did not respond. No claim about who the funders are unless the piece documents it. Datelined London.

stories.label: Fed seen skipping October rate hike as job market cools
stories.summary: US employers added just 29,000 jobs in September against the 90,000 economists expected, the Labor Department reported, and traders now expect the Federal Reserve to skip a rate rise in October. Lead with the US jobs number against the forecast and the unemployment rate, then what it does to the Fed rate: the Fed has been raising rates against war-driven energy inflation, and a labour market this weak makes another rise harder to justify. The mechanism and who pays: the central bank is caught between prices pushed up by the Hormuz shock, which rate rises cannot fix, and hiring that is already stalling — stagflation in plain terms — and its choice sets borrowing costs far beyond the US, including for dollar-indebted emerging economies. Give the market reaction in the US 10-year Treasury yield and the dollar if Reuters states it, the date of the next Fed meeting, and Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan's view that more rises are needed (Bloomberg) as the counterpoint. Only figures the sources carry. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Trump vs Europe as US presses for release of emergency diesel stocks
stories.summary: Third story in the diesel arc; Trump's ultimatum (10-01) and the US demand ahead of the EU meeting (this morning) are covered — one clause each. The new development is Europe's answer: EU officials held an emergency call, and France has proposed a fresh coordinated release of diesel and crude by the EU and the International Energy Agency (Bloomberg). Lead with the French proposal — how many barrels, from whose stocks, over what period — and which governments back or resist it. The mechanism: emergency stocks exist for supply cuts, and Europe is being pushed to spend them to lower prices in the country that supplies about half its diesel imports; every barrel released now is one not available if US exports actually stop. Say how many days of cover the EU holds and what a release would leave. Then the decision still open: what the EU must agree, and by when. RT is in the cluster — do not write from it. Datelined Brussels, or Paris if the proposal is the lead.

stories.label: Manchester City ignites tension: the UAE warns Britain of the repercussions of the penalty
stories.summary: This is an economy story, not a sports one: the United Arab Emirates has warned Britain that it could scale back its investments in the country depending on how harshly Manchester City — owned by Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Mansour — is punished for the financial breaches an independent Premier League commission found it guilty of this week, Bloomberg reported. Goal.com is relaying Bloomberg: write 'Bloomberg reported' and attribute the warning to its sources, not as confirmed fact. Lead with the warning and who it was delivered to (the feed tags Downing Street and Prime Minister Andy Burnham), then the scale of what is at stake: Emirati investment in Britain as the sources quantify it. The mechanism: a sovereign investor is using capital flows as leverage over a private sporting tribunal, which tests whether a regulator's ruling can stand when the defendant's owner is a state the government needs. Give the government's and the Premier League's replies, and what penalties the commission can impose. No match or squad detail. Datelined London.

stories.label: NA body seeks Rs5,000 wheat support price for Rabi season
stories.summary: A National Assembly standing committee has recommended that Pakistan's federal government fix a minimum support price for wheat of Rs5,000 per 40kg or more for the 2026-27 Rabi season, with one subsidy mechanism for farmers nationwide. Lead with the figure and what it would change: say what farmers were paid last season and whether a support price currently exists, as Dawn states it. The mechanism: a guaranteed price decides how much wheat is sown in the weeks ahead, so it is a food-security decision for a country of 240 million with inflation above 10% (covered this morning — one clause); but a state-set price is also a subsidy, and Islamabad's room to pay one is limited by its IMF programme — say so only if Dawn does. Name who pays either way: growers squeezed by fertiliser and diesel costs, or urban households buying flour. This is a committee recommendation, not a decision — say who decides and when sowing starts. Reference the wheat price for the reader's chart. Datelined Islamabad.

stories.label: OpenAI shows three staff the door over alleged information misuse
stories.summary: OpenAI has fired two safety researchers and a program manager for allegedly mishandling confidential company information, the company confirmed to The Register after an internal investigation. Lead with who was dismissed — two of the three worked on safety — and what OpenAI says they did, in its words; then what is not known: what the information was, who received it, and whether the three dispute the account (the feed tags The Wall Street Journal and Hugging Face — say what role each plays only as the article states). The mechanism the reader should see: the people best placed to say whether a frontier AI lab's systems are safe are bound by its confidentiality rules, so the line between a leak and a warning is drawn by the employer. Say whether any of the three claims whistleblower status and what protection US law gives AI-lab staff, if The Register covers it. These are the company's allegations — attribute them. Datelined San Francisco.

stories.label: Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what's true | New Scientist
stories.summary: The AI maths results announced in recent months rest on formalisation — translating a proof into code that a proof-checking program verifies — and New Scientist reports that this foundation has recently come under strain (the feed tags software bugs and the checker's kernel: say exactly what was found, in which system, and by whom). Lead with the concrete problem, not the 'battle' framing: what flaw or dispute emerged, and which claimed results it touches. The reader is technical: explain in one plain sentence what a proof assistant's kernel is and why everything depends on it — a machine-checked proof is only as sound as the few thousand lines that do the checking, and an AI system optimising to make the checker say 'yes' will find its bugs rather than a proof. Then who decides what counts as proved: the companies announcing results, or the mathematicians maintaining the tools. State what has and has not been invalidated. Write it as news of the finding, not a feature. Dateline the city of the institution or project the article centres on.

stories.label: Who gets to decide if AI is safe? Africa wants a say
stories.summary: African leaders are pressing at the UN Security Council for a say in how AI safety is defined and governed, while African companies race to adopt American and Chinese models with little attention paid to safety, Rest of World reports. The feed entry is a teaser, so keep strictly to what the full page states. Lead with the concrete act: which governments or leaders, in what forum, asking for what — a seat, a standard, a fund. The mechanism: safety testing is done by and for the countries that build the models — in their languages, against their risks — so the continent that imports the systems inherits evaluations that never examined its languages, its elections or its payment systems, and has no vote on the rules. Name the African institutions doing safety work and what they lack, and what the US and China answered. Africa here is the actor, not the setting. Dateline the African city the reporting centres on, otherwise New York for the Security Council.
